title: Man City Player Ratings vs. Aston Villa: Perfect Record Evaporates in Error-Strewn Display
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray9:50 AM EDTMan City suffered their first league defeat of the season. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesManchester City’s perfect Premier League record was extinguished on Saturday as they were beaten 2–1 by Aston Villa following a Nicolas Jackson brace.

The guilty verdict continues to loom over the Cityzens, repeatedly throwing into question what their Premier League matches really mean until a punishment is laid out, but they had little time for existential thoughts after falling behind to Jackson’s terrific opener in just the sixth minute.

City responded impressively at Villa Park, albeit without being able to find an equalizer before the break. They frequently forced Zion Suzuki into athletic saves either side of two half-hearted penalty appeals, and Iliman Ndiaye came closest when his wicked strike crashed off the outside of the post.

The visitors continued to pile on pressure after the restart and were swiftly rewarded when Erling Haaland’s towering header brought them level. But their joy was short-lived as Villa retook the lead when Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to rebuff Jackson’s fizzing drive.

Despite huffing and puffing for an equalizer to preserve their unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign, City ultimately came up short against a resilient Villa rearguard—and that leaves the door ajar for title rivals Arsenal to move level on points with them at the summit.

Iliman Ndiaye was lively in the Midlands. / Martin Rickett/PA Images/Getty ImagesWhile not City’s sleekest display of the current campaign, there were some encouraging individual showings worthy of praise. Iliman Ndiaye is one of those who stood out, taking advantage of Villa’s willingness to funnel the ball into wide areas when defending.

The summer recruit’s quick feet and explosive acceleration was City’s greatest outlet, so it was little surprise to see their equalizer stem from his creativity. An inch-perfect delivery into the penalty area found the grateful head of Haaland.
There were other moments of invention from Ndiaye, who enjoyed darting inside and taking aim. One of those efforts thwacked the woodwork, while another was impressively saved by Suzuki.

A tough day for Guéhi. / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesIt’s been a tumultuous period for Marc Guéhi since City’s guilty verdict. Whether the ruling has had any genuine influence on his performances is unclear, but he’s been making errors for club and country regardless. After a disastrous mistake for England in its 3–2 defeat to Spain in late September, the center back gifted Jackson his opener at Villa Park almost exactly a month later.

An extremely poor touch from Enzo Fernández’s lofted pass across the defense ricocheted into the path of John McGinn, who in turn found Jackson. The finish was instinctive and clinical, but there would have been no such opportunity without Guéhi’s costly blunder—one of many instances where City, and Guéhi more specifically, struggled to handle the ex-Chelsea forward.
As Villa’s goalkeeper Suzuki continually proved his worth with some fantastic saves, Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to match the quality of his opposite number.

The Italian was undoubtedly at fault for Jackson’s second goal. Sure, the shot was struck with ferocity, but it was incredibly central when squirming beneath Donnarumma’s body. Not for the first time, the City stopper finds himself under the microscope.
Haaland did what Haaland does best. / Molly Darlington/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Gianluigi Donnarumma—3.9: Absolutely had to save from Jackson on the hour. Simply not good enough from a supposedly elite goalkeeper.
RB: Abdukodir Khusanov—8.1: Shifted into central defense after halftime following an entertaining battle up against the eye-catching Johan Manzambi. Proved an upgrade on Guéhi.

CB: Marc Guéhi—5.2: Moved to the right side of defense by Enzo Maresca, which seemed to rattle him. Consistently struggled in battles with the lively Jackson, alongside making the mistake which offered Villa their early lead. Withdrawn at halftime, too.
CB: Rúben Dias—6.2: One absolutely vital intervention denied an almost certain goal during the first half, but, like his teammates, he sometimes found life hard against Villa’s direct forwards.

LB: Joško Gvardiol—7.3: Caused issues by Alysson, who was desperate to dribble at every opportunity, but at least provided some serious attacking threat. Gvardiol would have been among the goals had it not been for several fantastic saves from Suzuki.

CM: Elliot Anderson—7.8: Such an impressive general in midfield, eating up ground and recovering possession with ease. Worth every penny of his $154 million fee—well, when it comes to modern transfer fees, at least.
